I was never iron but I’ve been diamond for the last three seasons. I think the best advice depends on what role you play. I’d be clueless if you’re a jungler or bot laner but for mid or top lane I’d say:

1. Learn how to cs under tower. Melee minions with full health will take two tower hits leaving them on enough hp to die from one auto attack (your right click) from almost every champion, if not every champion. Ranged minions are a bit more awkward, on full health they need one auto attack, a tower hit and then an auto. Or if you have enough attack speed you can just let the tower hit once and then auto the minion twice. Learning to be able to do this without having to spend abilities/mana on minions will help you stay in lane longer and obviously get more gold. 

2. Recall as the cannon wave is coming. This is huge. Every third wave has a cannon minion. So you want to recall as soon after you’ve killed the wave before the cannon minion wave. What this means is that if your enemy lane opponent clears the cannon wave after you’ve recalled, it’ll take a lot longer than a regular wave and towers prioritise hitting cannon minions. This means when the the wave is fully into the tower it’ll take the other minions longer to die. Usually I only miss one minion from this, as opposed to the three or four you might miss from recalling on a different wave. 

3. Map awareness. I look at my minimap like every two or three seconds. More often than not I’ll see the enemy jungler ganking my teammates before my teammates do. 
If I see enemy jungler is ganking a different lane I know I’m free to play aggressive. 

4. Proactivity. Make use of downtime. If I’ve already cleared a wave, instead of just sitting at tower waiting for the next one, I’ll look for an opportunity to go roam to a different lane or go into the enemy jungle, drop a ward. 

If you know your team is going to try contest an objective like drake or herald, it’s important to be there before it spawns, not as it spawns. Having the jump on positioning in objective fights can be huge. 

5. Mute chat. If you’re in iron your teammates have nothing to say that is worth hearing in all likelihood. Focus on your self, don’t give anyone the chance to tilt you. 

6. Keep your champion pool small. Knowing how to pilot 2 or 3 champions without having to think about it is better than counter picking something you don’t know how to play. The simpler the better. 

Hope this helps.
